classification.difficultyReason: Find two rotation centres by considering both endpoint correspondences and intersecting their perpendicular bisectors.

inlines.text: shown can be rotated to the line segment

. How would you find the other centre of rotation?

spec.description: Coordinate axes with positive arrowheads, no ticks or grid, and two coloured endpoint-labelled segments. Labels and axes are black; the segment colours distinguish the two figures.
spec.mathematics: A=(-3,1), B=(-1,2), C=(2,4), D=(3,2). AB rises to the right and CD falls to the right. Both segments have length sqrt(5).
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied coordinates and segments are visible; rotation centres and perpendicular bisectors are absent.

inlines.text: Intersect the perpendicular bisectors of BC and AD, then those of AC and BD.

answer.worked:
A rotation centre lies on the perpendicular bisector of each point and its image.

For $B\mapsto C$ and $A\mapsto D$, the midpoint of $BC$ is $(\frac12,3)$ and its gradient is $\frac23$. Its perpendicular bisector is
$$\begin{align*}y-3&=-\frac32\left(x-\frac12\right)\\y&=-\frac32x+\frac{15}{4}.\end{align*}$$
The midpoint of $AD$ is $(0,\frac32)$ and its gradient is $\frac16$. Its perpendicular bisector is $y=-6x+\frac32$.
$$\begin{align*}-\frac32x+\frac{15}{4}&=-6x+\frac32\\\frac92x&=-\frac94\\x&=-\frac12\\y&=-6\left(-\frac12\right)+\frac32\\y&=\frac92.\end{align*}$$
The first centre is $\left(-\frac12,\frac92\right)$.

For $A\mapsto C$ and $B\mapsto D$, the midpoint of $AC$ is $(-\frac12,\frac52)$ and its gradient is $\frac35$. Its perpendicular bisector is
$$\begin{align*}y-\frac52&=-\frac53\left(x+\frac12\right)\\y&=-\frac53x+\frac53.\end{align*}$$
Since $BD$ is horizontal with midpoint $(1,2)$, its perpendicular bisector is $x=1$.
$$\begin{align*}y&=-\frac53(1)+\frac53\\y&=0.\end{align*}$$
The second centre is $(1,0)$. The endpoint vectors about the first centre turn $90^\circ$ anticlockwise; those about the second turn $90^\circ$ clockwise. Thus both intersections give the required rotations.
